purpose: the repair_v7 injection driver did not record which truth-side f_bin model it used: the --fbin-model flag was added in the same commit that launched the run, and the provenance field was omitted.  This verifies from the OUTPUTS that the pre-registered extended model was applied.  The driver has since been patched to record it directly for future runs.
method: realized binary fraction per true mass from one repair_v7 node, tested against the pre-registered extended_binary_fraction under binomial sampling with n = N_INJECT_PER_MASS per mass
why_one_node_not_an_average: every node is generated from a fresh default_rng(SEED) on the same MASS_GRID, so the binary draws are IDENTICAL across nodes of a branch -- verified here.  Averaging over nodes therefore does not reduce sampling noise, and a tolerance derived as if it did would be far too tight.  An earlier version of this check used a flat 0.03 tolerance on that mistaken assumption and reported a spurious FAIL.

goodness_of_fit.interpretation: chi2 = 41.2 on 45 masses with p = 0.63, and the mean z of +0.13 shows no systematic offset.  The largest single deviation, |z| = 3.17, is the expected maximum over 45 independent binomial draws.  The extended model was applied exactly as pre-registered.

control_check: repair_v6 nodes realize a flat ~0.41 at every mass, confirming the constant model there and that the two versions differ only in f_bin
